statement: An explicit boundary-fixed disk loop generates a transitive group with full interior centralizer exactly a closed free proper copy of R. Two actual principal sections of this same action are related by (s,t) -> (s-t^3,t). The literal linear interpolation in the second section has an explicit midpoint whose conjugate has no continuous extension at any original boundary point. Consequently that midpoint has no uniform filled-orbit bound from any compact family of original boundary-fixed maps and any finite word length. The original loop itself has an explicit operator-preserving relative contraction.
depends_on: C72 exact spiral coordinate and uniform bounded-displacement boundary estimate; C33 actual principal action coordinates; C70 planar filled hull contained in convex hull; all actual loop, section, full-centralizer, interpolation and boundary-limit calculations proved here
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), exact actual-boundary comparison for one-dimensional proper operator groups.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The same actual Q-action, its two sections, and both coordinate inverses are explicit. The failed candidate is the stated coordinate interpolation, and its two distinct limits at each boundary point are proved by exact formulas and integral inequalities.
computational_checks: code/part_b/c74_principal_interpolation_certificate.py and adjacent JSON/stdout pass 41 exact symbolic and rational checks. No floating-point calculation supports the proof.
notes: The original loop is transitive on the interior and has full interior centralizer R. Scaling its three out-and-back amplitudes gives a valid relative contraction. The failure concerns interpolation in the displayed changed principal section, including every proposed fixed finite compact-word filled-hull bound for that candidate. No failure of a section-adapted contraction, no nontrivial centralizer homotopy class, and no completion of the general C12 problem are asserted.
